message.content:
Below is a quick “ready‑to‑run” example that pulls the first 25 resolution records for the IP **67.89.0.1** from VirusTotal.  
Feel free to copy‑paste it into a terminal (curl) or a Python script.

---

## 1️⃣  Using `curl`

```bash
curl -s \
  -H "x-apikey: sec_key5" \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25" \
  | jq .
```

* `-s` – silent mode (no progress bar).  
* `-H "x-apikey: sec_key5"` – your API key (replace with your own if needed).  
* `jq .` – pretty‑prints the JSON response (install `jq` if you don’t have it).

> **Tip:** If you want to see the raw JSON without pretty‑printing, just drop the `| jq .` part.

---

## 2️⃣  Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "sec_key5"
IP = "67.89.0.1"
LIMIT = 25

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/resolutions"
headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}
params = {"limit": LIMIT}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
response.raise_for_status()          # will raise an exception for HTTP errors

data = response.json()
print(data)                          # prints the full JSON payload
```

> **Requirements:**  
> ```bash
> pip install requests
> ```

---

## 3️⃣  What you’ll get back

The API returns a JSON object that looks roughly like this:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "67.89.0.1",
      "type": "resolutions",
      "attributes": {
        "ip_address": "67.89.0.1",
        "last_resolved": "2026-10-04T12:34:56Z",
        "resolved_ip": "192.0.2.123",
        "resolved_hostname": "example.com"
      }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 123,
      "limit": 25,
      "offset": 0,
      "next": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25&offset=25"
    }
  }
}
```

* `data` – an array of resolution objects (up to 25 per request).  
* `meta.pagination` – lets you know how many total records exist and gives you the URL for the next page if you want more.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Replace `sec_key5` with your own key if you’re not using that one. |
| ✅ | Adjust `LIMIT` if you want fewer or more than 25 records. |
| ✅ | Use the `next` link in `meta.pagination` to fetch subsequent pages. |

That’s all you need to pull the first 25 resolution records for the IP address. Happy hunting!
